name: Famicom (NES)
blurb: Nintendo's 1983 home console, sold in the West as the NES
title: Famicom: When It Came Out, Price and Classic Games
description: The Famicom (Family Computer) is Nintendo's home console, launched in Japan in 1983 for 14,800 yen and sold abroad as the NES. Production ended in 2003.
answer: The Famicom, short for Family Computer, is the home video game console Nintendo released in Japan on July 15, 1983, for 14,800 yen. A redesigned version, the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES), followed in North America in 1985–86, and together they sold about 61.91 million units. Nintendo stopped making the Famicom in 2003 and ended repairs in 2007; today it lives on through collectors, a 2016 mini re-release and Nintendo's online service.

body: The Japanese Famicom is a small white console with dark red trim, which is why Chinese players call it the "red and white machine" (红白机). The two controllers are wired straight into the console and slot into holders on its sides when not in use. Controller II has no Start or Select button but has a built-in microphone, which only a few games used. Games came on cartridges that plug into the top.

Masayuki Uemura led the design. Nintendo president Hiroshi Yamauchi reportedly chose the red, white and gold colors after seeing them on a billboard for an antenna company, and because his favorite scarf used the same scheme. For America the console was reworked into the grey, boxy NES with a front-loading slot.

body: Nintendo never officially sold the Famicom in mainland China, and imports were far too expensive for most families. Chinese factories filled the gap with cheap compatible clones that played the same cartridges, the best known being Subor (小霸王), later sold with a keyboard as an "educational computer". Wikipedia cites about 30 million clone units sold in China by late 1995, so for many Chinese children of the 1990s, "Famicom" meant a clone and a multi-game cartridge.

Original Famicoms and NES consoles are only found second-hand or in collections. The Classic Mini was discontinued in 2017, briefly brought back in 2018 and then stopped again. A selection of Famicom/NES games is included in Nintendo Switch Online.

faq.q: When did the Famicom come out?
faq.a: July 15, 1983 in Japan. The NES version had a test launch in New York in October 1985 and a nationwide US release in 1986.

faq.q: Is the Famicom the same as the NES?
faq.a: They play the same games but differ in shape, cartridge size and region. The Famicom is the Japanese original; the NES is the redesigned Western version.
Nintendo sold about 61.91 million Famicom and NES consoles worldwide, not counting the many clones.
